newsitem.title: ITALY: Main Italian force to leave for Albania on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Main Italian force to leave for Albania on Tuesday.

text.p: The main bulk of the Italian force which will spearhead a multinational security mission in Albania, will start moving to the small Balkan state from Tuesday, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Saturday.

Addressing the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), Prodi said a small contingent of Italian soldiers were already in Albania, but said the main force would be deployed over 10 days. Italy has committed about 2,500 troops to the United Nations-sanctioned operation.

Troops from France, Greece, Spain, Turkey and Romania are also taking part in the force, which will be around 6,000 strong. An advance party of 20 Italian troops arrived in the Western Albanian port of Durres on Friday.
Italy has been asked to led the operation which is designed to assist delivery of relief aid to Albania, brought to the brink of collapse by an armed insurrection last month.

"Even if some of our soldiers are already in Albania, the main structure of our mission will leave on Tuesday and over the following 10 days," Prodi said, adding that wanted to set up a parliamentary committee to monitor the mission.
Officials had indicated earlier that the Italian force was expected to be deployed from Monday onwards. The transfer of soldiers is being coordinated from the southeastern Italian port of Brindisi.
